document.abstract: Today's workflows require the use of various acquisition and data sources. In order to keep the acquired data formats compatible with traditional film acquisition, some major problems need to be addressed. First, when acquisition is done via digital camera and traditional film camera, the final cut between shots often shows dramatic differences in color, depth of field, and quality. Studies will be presented about digital camera shots (HD material), acquired with a functional model of a digital film style camera. Second, in post-production most facilities have to work with scanned material that comes from various sources (telecines, scanners). This often results in differences in colors and dynamic range. Technologies that can be used to compensate between different source materials will be discussed. Finally, colors are the most crucial element in a hybrid production chain. Preserving colors from acquisition, scanning, recording, and projection is one of the most sophisticated tasks during production. Color management will be considered as a throughput solution.

authors.bio: Elfi Bernt works as product manager, Arriscan, in the Business Unit Digital Systems' of Arnold & Richter (ARRI). She graduated from the University of Darmstadt in 1994 with a degree in computer science and joined ARRI in 2003. Her main responsibilities are product management tasks for the Arriscan and the ARRI CMS. Before joining ARRI, Bernt worked for Discreet. She brought a strong post-production background and knowledge of working with high-end post-production systems into the team. She understands the challenges of today's digital intermediate requirements and supports the development team of the Arriscan by bringing client feedback and market experience to the development team.
authors.name: E. Bernt

authors.bio: Michael Koppetz is a senior engineer in the R&D department at ARRI. He graduated from the Technical University of Munich in 1986 with a degree in mechanical engineering and joined ARRI in the same year. In the course of his career, he took on the responsibility of the optical and mechanical design group at ARRI's Munich facility and was project leader for several new camera products. With the general reorientation of ARRI's R&D activities, Koppetz moved the focus of his work away from the traditional products and today is intensively involved in the company's development of digital camera technologies, contributing expertise based on his background in the design of professional film cameras.
authors.name: M. Koppetz

authors.bio: Peter Geissler is project manager in the R&D department at ARRI, where he is responsible for the development of the ARRI color management system. Geissler graduated from the University of Heidelberg in 1998 with a Ph.D. in physics. After joining ARRI in 1999, he worked on the Arrilaser and Arriscan image processing, calibration, and color management. He has a strong background in image science and is co-editor of the Handbook of Computer Vision and Applications.
authors.name: P. Geissler

authors.bio: Sibylle Maier is product manager for the Arrilaser. She graduated from the Polytechnics in Cologne in 1996 with a degree in photo engineering and joined ARRI in the same year. During her studies she developed the idea of film acquisition while working as a camera assistant, and later film post-production, while working as a service engineer for Avid. After gathering experience in the digital effects work at ARRI digital film, she joined the development group of the Arrilaser at its inception.
authors.name: S. Maier

authors.bio: Tran Quoc Khanh graduated from the Technical University of Ilmenau/Germany with an optical engineering degree and a Ph.D. degree in optical spectroscopy, in 1985 and 1989, respectively. Khanh joined ARRI in 2000. He is responsible for the development of the optical parts in the new digital motion picture HDTV-camera, film scanner, recorder, and film projector of ARRI.
authors.name: T. Q. Khanh
